https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/12/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter: Döntött a kormány, fenékküszöbbel és annak kiépítéséig két elsüllyeszthető bárkával emelnék a Duna vízszintjét Belföld Nádor András Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Egy dunai fenékküszöb építésének azonnali megkezdését és ezzel párhuzamosan egy ideiglenes megoldás előkészítését rendeltük el – mondta Magyar Péter szerdai rendkívüli tájékoztatóján. Ideiglenes megoldásként két, potenciálisan elsüllyeszthető, 80 méteres bárkát fognak készenlétbe helyezni Paksnál. A beruházást a sürgőssége miatt kiemeltnek minősítette a kormány, hatmilliárd forintba fog kerülni. A miniszterelnök bejelentette: ha elkészül a fenékküszöb, akár egy méterrel is képes lesz megemelni a vízszintet a területen. „A kormány a mai helyszínbejárást követően a vízügyi, energetikai és védelmi szakemberek egybehangzó javaslata alapján meghozta a döntést arról, hogy haladéktalanul, már a holnapi napon megkezdjük a Duna két partjától, a paksi atomerőmű és Dunaszentbenedek település között egy Dunai fenékküszöb építését, első körben 35 ezer, majd 110 ezer köbméter kő felhasználásával.” A miniszterelnök szerint a beruházással „pár héten belül biztosítható, hogy a Dunai vízszint az atomerőmű hűtőcsatornájánál ne csökkenjen mínusz 90 cm alá, és ennek következtében Magyarország legfontosabb erőműve teljes kapacitással működhessen”. Bejelentette azt a kormánydöntést is, hogy „a várhatóan ismét rendkívül gyorsan apadó vízszint miatt” a fenékküszöb építésével párhuzamosan készenlétbe helyeznek Paksnál két 80 méter hosszúságú bárkát. „Szükség esetén készen állunk arra, hogy ezen két bárka irányított elsüllyesztésével rövid távon akár 20 centimétert emeljünk a Duna vízszintjén, hogy ezzel a végleges fenékküszöb elkészültéig is elkerülhető legyen a paksi erőmű teljes leállítása.” Magyar azt mondta, a két beavatkozás, a fenékküszöb építése és a bárkák készenlétbe helyezése egymást fogja kiegészíteni. Szerinte jelenleg ez a leghatékonyabb és legbiztonságosabb megoldás, és ezt támogatják a szakértők és a hatóságok is. A védelmi és kivitelezési munkálatok koordinálásával és irányításával Kádár Pál tábornokot, a Védelmi Igazgatási Hivatal vezetőjét bízta meg a miniszterelnök. A kormányfő szerint már ma este Paksra érkezik az ideiglenes megoldáshoz szükséges egyik 80 méteres bárka Mohácsról, és holnap már a második is itt lesz. Szerdán derült ki, hogy felterjesztéssel fordult a paksi önkormányzat a magyar kormányhoz, amelyben azt kérték, a megváltozott klimatikus viszonyok miatt a kormány vizsgálja felül a paksi atomerőmű hosszú távú biztonságos hűtővízellátását garantáló valamennyi lehetséges megoldást. Barnabás István, Paks alpolgármestere a felterjesztés tartalmáról azt mondta, az önkormányzat nem egy konkrét műszaki megoldást javasol, hanem a szóba jöhető javaslatok vizsgálatát, és az alacsony vízállásból eredő problémák megoldását kéri. Magyar Péter kedden közölte, hogy szerdán a paksi atomerőműben ülésezik a kormány . Szerdai posztjából derült ki, hogy a buszozó miniszterekkel ellentétben ő helikopterrel ment a kormányülésre. Magyar még hétfőn jelentette be, hogy visszakapcsolták az atomerőmű kettes blokkjának hármas turbináját, így ismét két turbina termel. Erre azért volt lehetőség, mert a Duna szintje 19 centiméterrel haladta meg az egy héttel ezelőtt mért mélypontot. A jelenlegi trend alapján ugyanakkor a vízcsökkenés után rendkívül alacsony szinten stagnál majd a vízállás , ráadásul a jövőben egyre többször számolhatunk majd azzal, hogy alig lesz víz a folyóinkban . https://www.dw.com/en/how-north-korea-ha.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IjBh North Korean leader Kim Jong Un (left) has profited greatly from cooperation with Russia Image: KCNA/KNS/AFP Advertisement For years, satellite images of North Korea at night showed only a few small patches of light. Electricity shortages meant that even cities remained dark. In the six years since April 2020, however, the illuminated area in the center of Pyongyang has tripled in size. The information portal NK News sees the increased illumination of the urban area as evidence that the regime has prioritized the supply of electricity to new streets and houses in the center to showcase its achievements. At the last party congress in 2021, Kim Jong Un , North Korea's leader, announced that he would build 50,000 new apartments in the capital. And he did embark on the plan: in the new neighborhood of Hwasong, for example, with the construction of two 40-story apartment blocks shaped like Hwasong intercontinental ballistic missiles. Why North Korea is now Europe's problem To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The new high-rise districts are not the only sign of North Korea's improved prosperity. People who have been visiting Pyongyang for a long time report that the city now appears more modern. There are many imported cars, including electric cars from China , smartphone apps with QR codes to make payments or to call taxis, and department stores that stock Western fashion brands and cosmetics. Pyongyang has transformed into a modern city thanks to North Korea's deals with Russia and China Image: Jon Chol Jin/AP Photo/picture alliance The regime has completed construction in Pyongyang of the biggest hospital in the country and a hothouse the size of New York's Central Park. In June 2025, Kim officially opened the five-kilometer-long (3.3 miles) beach resort of Wonsan-Kalma on the east coast, with space for 20,000 guests. In June, the Wall Street Journal described North Korea as the "world's most unlikely growth story." North Korea's lucrative war deals with Russia The dictatorship is presumably able to finance this sudden upturn thanks to the substantial income from its involvement in Russia's war against Ukraine . According to a report by the South Korean Institute for National Security Strategy (INSS) in March, North Korea earns between $7.7 billion and $14.4 billion (€6.7 billion and €12.5 billion) from the sale of munitions to Moscow and the deployment of troops. Bloomberg Economics recently estimated that between 2022 and 2025, North Korea earned more than $14 billion by providing military support for Russia. North Korea expands its role in Russia's war against Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Furthermore, it brought in another $8 billion through trade with China , the provision of North Korean workers to other countries, export business and online criminality. The hacking of the ByBit platform in February 2025 was one of the world's biggest cryptocurrency heists. Suspected North Korean hackers made off with $1.5 billion worth of Ethereum, a network with its own virtual currency. In comparison: the previous year, North Korea's entire GDP was $27 billion. North Korea's involvement in Russia's war effort It is unclear whether it was Russia or North Korea who first had the idea of using the impoverished country's massive stockpiles of munitions in Russia's war against Ukraine. Kyiv estimates that in 2024 and 2025, North Korea supplied half the munitions Russia used at the front, as well as self-propelled guns, multiple rocket launchers and ballistic missiles. Ukraine says North Korea is currently planning to transfer a missile unit to Russia to fight against Ukraine, consisting of 90 soldiers, six launch pads and up to 120 missiles. Between 16,000 and 22,000 North Korean soldiers are already helping Russia to drive Ukraine out of the border province of Kursk and clear the area of mines afterward. According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , Kim now intends to station a further 30,000 to 50,000 soldiers in Russia. Kim hails troops returning from Russia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The business is a lucrative one: The INSS report says that, every month, Kim receives $2,800 per North Korean soldier, $3,000 for an officer and $6,000 to $10,000 for every soldier killed in action. As in Soviet times, the reciprocal arrangement is conducted primarily through exchange transactions. In exchange for munitions, arms and soldiers, Russia supplies North Korea with crude oil and oil products, grain and military goods from anti-aircraft systems to the technologies for building drones, missiles and submarines. North Korea's new global stage Kim's new role as Russia's supporter has given him greater political importance and military power, as demonstrated by the launch of two 5,000-ton destroyers. In all 15 of the years he has been in power, the autocratic leader has never had this much influence, or this much money. North Korea gains critical intel by aiding Russia in Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video It's an astonishing turnaround. Kim noticeably lost weight during the COVID-19 pandemic , and at the Workers' Party congress in 202,1 he shed tears as he admitted that the national economic development strategy had fallen "far short in almost all sectors." At the next party congress five years later, with seven rows of artillery pieces lined up outside the building, Kim crowed, "Everything has fundamentally changed." The partnership with Russia has allowed North Korea to shed its status as a pariah of world politics and overcome its isolation. In June 2024, the Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Kim in Pyongyang . Chinese leader Xi Jinping came in June of this year , three months after the Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko . In September 2025, Kim was in attendance at the celebrations in Beijing , alongside Xi and Putin, to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II . Profits not reaching North Koreans However, observers say this economic upswing is not benefiting the majority of the population. Many households already in a precarious situation and without access to foreign currency have been hit hard by rising food prices and the devaluation of the won, the national currency. In many families, the women, too, must now go out to work in order to maintain living standards. In the spring of 2024, Kim promoted a "20x10" development program for regions beyond the well-supplied capital Pyongyang. Presumably, he intends to finance this with the new additional revenue. The plan foresees that modern factories will be built in 20 cities or regions annually, creating 200 regional industrial projects over 10 years. But according to Andrei Lankov, a professor and North Korea expert at Kookmin University in Seoul, the majority of the 20x10 projects fail. "This is because not only do the factories have no infrastructure, they also do not take into account the mechanisms for supplying electricity, equipment, and raw materials," he said. The factories are operated according to the principles of a planned economy, which is unsuited to small and medium-sized businesses. "Unlike the economic growth that took place in North Korea in the mid-2010s, the current growth was based not on internal economic reforms, but only on international good fortune," Lankov said. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-boost.text: The EU is weighing closer economic cooperation with the U.K. to reduce dependence on hostile powers and trade rivals, one of the top politicians responsible for the negotiations said Tuesday, a decade after Britain left the bloc. Speaking at POLITICO’s Playbook Live Summit in Brussels, Finnish MEP Mika Aaltola — a member of the European People’s Party and vice-chair of the Parliament’s delegation for relations with the U.K. — said the EU is at “the conceptual drawing board” stage when it comes to relations with like-minded partners. While Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced an “associate membership” bid for Canada in her State of the Union speech, Aaltola said that “clearly, now things are being a little bit discussed when it comes to [the] U.K.” Advertisement Advertisement This, he said, could include “sectoral” deals, or “some kind of a market freedom of markets type of arrangement, like with Switzerland.” “We need these visions because we are stuck, pretty much,” he added, between threats from Russia and increasingly tense relations with U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration. “The world order is changing in front of our eyes. U.S.A. is losing a war with Iran. Russia is losing a war. You know, great powers are actually losing positions.” Von der Leyen’s offer to Canada, as Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government navigates an escalating trade war with Washington, is part of a push for stronger relations with democratic, pro-free-trade states. However, Brussels has been quick to play down the prospects of the U.K. being offered associate membership , which it says is reserved for countries that cannot geographically join the EU. The U.K. and EU have long been planning a summit designed to reset relations. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said at the United Nations in New York: “Our focus at the moment is on a U.K.-EU summit which we hope will take place later this year.”
